stimulus.text:
| Power | National government | State governments | Both |
|---|---|---|---|
| Levy taxes |  |  | X |
| Coin money | X |  |  |
| Regulate trade between the states | X |  |  |
| Establish public schools |  | X |  |
| Declare war | X |  |  |
| Establish courts |  |  | X |
| Make treaties with other nations | X |  |  |
stimulus.source_note: Table drawn from the Constitution: Article I, Section 8 (national powers), Article I, Section 10 (powers forbidden to the states), and the Tenth Amendment (powers reserved to the states).

source: original; table drawn from the Constitution — Article I, Sections 8 and 10, and the Tenth Amendment.

books.section: Topic 3.9 The Constitution, Federalism—the National Government and the States

primary_sources: Constitution of the United States, Article I, Sections 8 and 10, and the Tenth Amendment (1787-1791)

stem: According to the table, which power shows that the states kept a real sphere of their own under the Constitution rather than becoming mere agents of the national government?

options.misconception: Coining money belongs to the national government alone, so it shows national power, not state power.
Declaring war belongs to the national government alone, so it shows national power, not state power.
Making treaties belongs to the national government alone, so it shows national power, not state power.

rationales.C: The table gives public schools to the states alone, so the states kept their own work to do.
rationales.A: Coining money sits in the national column, so it cannot show state power.
rationales.B: Declaring war sits in the national column, so it cannot show state power.
rationales.D: Making treaties sits in the national column, so it cannot show state power.
rationales.general:
1. The table divides powers between the national government, the states, and both.
2. A state-only row is the proof that the states kept work of their own.
3. Coining money, declaring war, and making treaties are all national-only rows.
4. Establishing public schools is the only state-only row, so it carries the point.
Remember: in a powers table, a row owned by one level alone shows that level kept its own sphere.
